thread.title: Prince William supervisors approve Hornbaker Road data center outside overlay district - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Prince William supervisors approve Hornbaker Road data center outside overlay district - NewsBreak

author: Sébastien Kraft
title: Prince William supervisors approve Hornbaker Road data center outside overlay district - NewsBreak
text:
By Sébastien Kraft ,
8 hours ago The Prince William Board of County Supervisors narrowly approved the Hornbaker Road data center near Innovation Town Center during its Tuesday night meeting, with agitated discussion marking the proceedings.
The board voted 4-3 in favor of the controversial tech hub, with Chair Deshundra Jefferson, Coles District Supervisor Yesli Vega and Gainesville Supervisor George Stewart dissenting.
As it was located outside the county's Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District, the project necessitated a rezoning application and special use permit, both of which passed by the 4-3 margin.
The rezoning involved a transition of just over 40 acres from A-1, agricultural and PBD, planned business district, to M-2, light industrial. It also involved a 91-foot landscaping and setback area, according to county staff, and located around 400-450 feet from nearby townhouses close to the Innovation Town Center.
Located in the Brentsville District, the project also needed an eleventh-hour pivot from Tom Gordy, the Brentsville supervisor and a frequent data center skeptic, to be approved.
Gordy's decision was fueled by a last-minute proffer addition regarding access to the nearby Pegasus substation and the prevention of additional power lines for the project, with the proffer mandating no new infrastructure. The board took a 10-minute recess late in Tuesday’s proceedings to rewrite the language therein.
The project applicants are cited as “MJV Parcel A, LLC” and “PWC – Parcel B, LLC,” in county documents.
“I don’t know whether [the proffer addition was] the determining factor or not,” Mark Looney, an attorney representing Mortenson Development, the contract purchaser of the property, told InsideNoVa following the meeting. “But we [know] when you come to these board meetings, you understand that transmission lines countywide are an issue – and for us with this particular application, we already have agreements in place that allow for the power to come directly to the site, and so therefore, we felt comfortable that we weren’t further contributing to the need for transmission lines other than the ones that the State Corporation Commission has already approved that would interact with that substation.”
While Vega remained mum despite her dissent, Jefferson and Stewart were unequivocal in their remarks.
“No matter how much you polish a piece of fecal matter, it’s still that,” Stewart said of the project. “Another egg in the wrong basket of diversification.”
Jefferson said the board “lacked the political will” to vote down the project and stressed the need to “just say no.” She also likened the proposal to “putting lipstick on a pig.”
Meanwhile, Kenny Boddye, the Occoquan supervisor, praised the employment center that the project would create – aligning with the county’s Comprehensive Plan and maintaining 250-300 jobs for chip manufacturing company MobileSentrix.
Several community members turned out during the board’s afternoon and evening sessions, lamenting the possibility of another data center outside the overlay as well as other energy constraints.
Data center overlay
Earlier in the day, the board initiated a Zoning Text Amendment by a 6-0 vote, with Jefferson abstaining. The move is meant to reduce data center development within the overlay.
The zoning text amendment would alter – but did not entirely remove – the overlay to subtract all elements that are not existing data centers or parcels that have a plan already in place to become a data center.
Only three categories will stay within the overlay: existing parcels with operational data centers; pieces of land purchased by developers and submitted to county planning; and by-right parcels that currently have a site plan submitted.
Other properties will be removed from the overlay, with the amendment still needing to be reviewed by staff and the county's Planning Commission, and scheduled for a future public hearing.
